industry.why: Underweight, from Neutral, on the special topic 'Why the Defence Industry de-rated from July to October 2026 while Theon's forecasts rose' and on the condition written on this row last week, which fired: a third reading at F with no demand read in the strategist sources. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the Researcher's report finds multiples cut while estimates held, the industry's premium over the STOXX 600 down from 60% to 12% (Bernstein, 9-Oct-26), exit multiples moving towards 13 times operating profit as the order boom gives way to execution (Jefferies, 28-Oct-26, 'Defense Likely at Peak Fundamentals vs. Aero'), and budgets converting slowly into contracts (German run-rate, Boxer approvals); the UK Budget funded the existing Defence Investment Plan but postponed the 3%-of-output decision to the 2027 Spending Review. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: F now, D prior; both sectors F. A government-contracted revenue line with a falling multiple is a Fragility case in this regime, not a defensive one. The sector rows split the view: Primes D (land and ammunition hit hardest), Non-primes C (electronics and optronics held up). One live holding, Theon (4.05%), judged in components 4 and 5; no Pool name sits here, so the Lists are unmoved. Counter-case: estimates have not fallen, the premium compression may already be the exit multiple, and German approvals may convert (Rheinmetall 5-Nov-26, Bundestag budget vote 27-Nov-26). Back to C if relative strength leaves F as approvals convert; to F on a signed Ukraine settlement followed by defence fund outflows.

sector.why: Neutral, carried, on the special topic 'Why the Defence Industry de-rated from July to October 2026 while Theon's forecasts rose': over three months to 28-Oct-26 the electronics and optronics names in this sector held up (MilDef, Hensoldt, Exail, Exosens) while short-cycle land and ammunition fell, so the Researcher's suggested split, long-cycle electronics over short-cycle land, is expressed by holding this row at Neutral while the industry and the Primes go to Underweight; the Fragility axis at Double Underweight already scores the small names' size and case risk, so no second penalty. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: F now, D prior, stated as a disagreement. One live holding, Theon (4.05%): its fall is mostly its own leverage priced against land-defence multiples, judged on its own case in component 5. Counter-case: three readings at F is the market's view of the whole industry. To D if relative strength stays F with the electronics names joining the fall.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No Swedish survey and no Riksbank reading reached the pack this week, so the condition for B (a confidence print at or above normal with the Riksbank on hold) could not be tested; the only Swedish data point is food retail volumes up 5.3% in September after a value-added tax cut (Danske, 18 Oct), which is a sector fact, not a country view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Four live holdings are Swedish (Avanza 0.50%, Hexatronic 4.95%, Sdiptech 5.05%, Xvivo 5.05%, 15.55 points), judged in component 4 and in amendment 10. Relative strength is not graded by country.
